source.author: cic
source.text: nam cum ita copulatae conexaeque sint, ut omnes omnium participes sint nec alia ab alia possit separari, tamen proprium suum cuiusque munus est, ut fortitudo in laboribus periculisque cernatur, temperantia in praetermittendis voluptatibus, prudentia in dilectu bonorum et malorum, iustitia in suo cuique tribuendo.
source.text_original: nam cum ita copulatae conexaeque sint, ut omnes omnium participes sint nec alia ab alia possit separari, tamen proprium suum cuiusque munus est, ut fortitudo in laboribus periculisque cernatur, temperantia in praetermittendis voluptatibus, prudentia in dilectu bonorum et malorum, iustitia in suo cuique tribuendo.
source.text_english: For since they are so joined and linked together that all share in all of them and one cannot be separated from another, still each has its own proper function: courage is seen in toil and dangers, temperance in passing over pleasures, prudence in the choice of goods and evils, justice in giving to each his own.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: quattuor uirtutes describunt Stoici ita sibi inuicem nexas et mutuo cohaerentes, ut, qui unam non habuerit, omnibus careat: prudentiam, iustitiam, fortitudinem, temperantiam.
reuse.text_original: quattuor uirtutes describunt Stoici ita sibi inuicem nexas et mutuo cohaerentes, ut, qui unam non habuerit, omnibus careat: prudentiam, iustitiam, fortitudinem, temperantiam.
reuse.text_english: The Stoics describe four virtues as so linked together and mutually interconnected that whoever does not possess one lacks them all: prudence, justice, courage, and temperance.
